Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the fuel cost for each km, the driver wage, the minutes late you accept, the free-delivery order value and the stall labour.
Keep Zones and Time windows up to date: the fee of each zone and the hours of each window are read by Orders, Pick-up shelf and the calculators.

Write each delivery on Deliveries with the zone, the time window, the driver, the km and the fee. The delivery flag and the fee for each km fill in, and the charts show zones, windows, weekdays and late minutes.

Write each run on Delivery runs with the stops, the km, the hours and the fees. The cost for each stop and whether the fees cover it fill in, and Driver hours shows the deliveries for each hour and the overtime.
Record every late or failed delivery on Late and failed with its reason and what was done. The cost of the redo, the credit to offer and the total loss fill in.
Use Pick-ups for the orders collected at the kitchen and Pick-up shelf for the orders waiting. The status, the hours until the slot and the balance to collect fill in.

Write each market or pop-up on Markets with the stall fee, the hours, the units brought and sold, the revenue and the costs. The profit, the sell-through (the share of what you brought that you sold) and a profit or loss flag fill in.
Plan the year on Event calendar with the stall fee and the application deadline, pack with Market packing list, and answer invitations on Pop-up requests with the break-even units.
Check Market stock plan and Market sales after each market: the leftover cost and the price for each unit show what to bring next time.
Add the vehicle costs of each month on Vehicle costs and the ratings on Delivery feedback to see the cost for each delivery and the rating trend.
Use the 14 calculators before you quote a fee, plan a route, plan market stock or decide on a stall: fee by zone, route, cost for each stop, market profit, break-even, packing and more.

Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages). Read the Delivery and Markets Dashboard and Charts every week.
Know which cafe or client has not paid and which account earns the most
Wholesale accounts, invoices and client payments for home bakeries
every product an account takes each week shows its value, its renewal date and a flag for a renewal that is near or missed
the weekly deliveries and the credit for returns give the invoice total, the due date and the sales tax in one calculator
Overdue invoice tracker with reminder steps
each invoice shows its days late and the amount outstanding, and the reminder step says which note to send or when to call
every credit and every returned or unsold product keeps its reason and its value, so the next invoice is right and the cause can be fixed
units, wholesale price, product cost and delivery handling give the margin of each account against your target, so a weak account is repriced
each late payment keeps the days late, the day you chased and the outcome, so you see who needs an early reminder
every client order shows the deposit, the balance outstanding and the days overdue, with the average days events take to pay
Cash due from invoices by week
open invoices and their due dates give the cash that is late now and the cash due in each of the next four weeks
each quarter the volume change, the margin and the decision are written down, and a margin below target is flagged for a price change
every cafe or shop you are courting shows its first contact, its trial order and the days it has waited

Order value from which a deposit is asked
The cafes and shops you supply and the prospects you are courting; the months together, the weekly value of the standing orders, the amount outstanding and the revenue of the last 12 months fill in.
Standing orders (the same products delivered every week)
One row for each product an account takes every week (the same products delivered every week) with the weekdays, price and renewal date; the weekly value, days to renewal and a flag fill in.
Weekly wholesale deliveries with the amount
One row for each standing order delivery with the day, the account, the product, the units and the price; the amount fills in, so the invoice at month end is a sum of real deliveries.
Monthly wholesale invoices with the days late
One row for each monthly invoice with the invoice date, the due date and the day it was paid; the amount outstanding, days late, days to pay and a timing flag fill in.
One row for each product on a monthly invoice with the units and the price; the line amount fills in, so you see which products carry each account.
Credit notes for returns and mistakes
One row for each credit note with the invoice, the reason and the amount; keep every credit in one place so the next invoice is right.
Returns and unsold products from accounts
One row for each return or unsold item an account sends back with the reason; the credit value at the wholesale price fills in.
Wholesale price list with the margin
Wholesale means selling to cafes and shops at a lower price: each product with its prices and cost; the discount and the margin (the share of the price left after costs) fill in.
Client payments by kind and method
One row for each payment from a client (deposit, balance, full payment or refund) with the method and the amount; the client phone fills in from the orders.
Client orders with the balance and the days overdue
One row for each client order with the total, the deposit (a part of the price paid to secure the date) and the day paid; the balance outstanding, days overdue and a flag fill in.
Late payer log with the outcome
One row for each late payment of an account or a client with the days late, the day you chased and what happened; the days to settle fill in, so you know who needs a reminder early.
One row for each reminder you sent to a client or an account with the channel and the tone; the days since the due date fill in, so you see how late the first reminder went.
One row for each call, visit or message with an account and what to do next; the days to the follow-up and a follow-up flag fill in, so no promise to an account is forgotten.
One row for each cafe or shop you are courting or have won, with the first contact and the trial order; the days open fill in for a prospect that is still waiting.
Sales by account for each month
One row for each account and month with the units and the amount, plus one row a month for all retail and event orders; the share of the month fills in.
One row for each quarterly review of an account with the change in volume, the margin and the decision; the price check and the days to the next review fill in.
Wholesale products and who buys them
The products you sell wholesale with the number of accounts that take each one and the units and value a week; all three fill in from the standing orders.
Standing order renewals with the new price
One row for each standing order renewal with the new price and your decision; the account, the old price, the price change and the days to the renewal fill in.
The days you give each account to pay and the most it may owe you; the amount outstanding, the room left and a hold flag fill in, so a new order is not accepted above the limit.

Standing order value a week by account
Type the units a week, the deliveries a week, the price and the cost; see the value of each delivery, the value a week, a month and a year, and the margin the standing order earns.
Monthly invoice builder with returns and due date
Type the units delivered in the month, the price, the units returned and the terms; see the sales, the credit for the returns, the invoice total with and without sales tax and the due date.
Invoice due date and late days
Type the invoice date, the terms and the amount; see the due date, the days until it is due or the days late, the amount overdue and what the wait has cost so far.
Cost of the wait so far
Type the days late and the amount; see which reminder to send now (friendly, second, a call or a pause of deliveries), the days to the next step and what the wait costs so far.
Credit note value and the new invoice total
Type the units returned, the price and the invoice total; see the credit, the share of the invoice, the credit with sales tax, the new invoice total and whether the owner must approve it.

Type the retail price, the wholesale discount and the cost for a unit; see the wholesale price, the margin, the price that keeps your target margin and the highest discount you can give.

Type the old price, the old cost and the change in ingredient costs; see the new cost, the margin you have now, the price that keeps the margin and the rise you can ask at the renewal.
Change in costs since the last price
Margin now at the old price
Credit limit check before a new order
Type what the account owes, its credit limit, the new order and the days its oldest invoice is late; see the amount owed after the order, the room left and whether to accept the order or hold it.
Days the oldest invoice is late
Largest new order you can accept
Type up to five open invoices with their amounts and due dates; see the cash that is late now and the cash due in each of the next four weeks and later.
Account value and rank among the accounts
Type the months, the units and the amount sold to an account; see the value and units each month, the price for a unit, its rank among your accounts and its share of wholesale revenue.
Deposit and balance status of a client order
Type the order total, what the client has paid and the due date; see the deposit to ask (a part of the price paid to secure the date), the balance, the share paid and the days overdue.
Type the amount, the days late and the minutes you spend chasing; see the cost of the money you wait for, the cost of the chasing, the total and whether waiting is still cheap.
Cost as a share of the amount
What-if: weekly units against wholesale price
Type the units a week, the wholesale price, the cost for a unit and the handling cost; read the monthly margin, then use the grid rows to see other units and prices for the same account.
